what_was_done: Each attempt now gets a fresh cmd lock: attach unlinks <key>.cmd.lock while it holds the job lock and before it spawns the worker, so an earlier attempt's escapee (a descendant that left its group with setsid and kept the inherited descriptor) holds only an unlinked inode and can neither delay the new worker's lock-taking nor authorise a kill for it. A worker that runs without the cmd lock now records no command_pgid (JobContext gets the note_command callback only when _take_cmd_lock returned a descriptor; the callback also writes the new command_started field, the moment the command was forked). Before the kill, attach compares the group leader's ps birth time with the record's command_started (falling back to started) via the new _leader_begun_near: a number reused after the recorded group died belongs to a leader born far from the record's time and is not signalled; unreadable ps output or a missing leader answers False, because a missed kill is safe. The claim in rewrite/spec/records/job.md is rewritten to match: fresh lock per attempt, the leader check before any kill, and neither field recorded by a lockless worker. Tests: test_escapee_of_an_earlier_attempt_neither_delays_nor_authorises runs the real worker with a command that spawns a setsid descendant holding the cmd lock descriptor, plants a stale running record naming a live unrelated group, and asserts the group survives, starts == 2 and elapsed < 5 s (the pre-fix code waited 5 s for the escapee's lock and killed the unrelated group); test_leader_begun_near_matches_the_ps_birth_time pins the helper (own group matches _now(), a 2020 stamp and a missing process do not); test_worker_without_the_cmd_lock_records_no_group makes <key>.cmd.lock unopenable and asserts the worker's record carries no command_pgid. Each fails against the mutated code (kill without the leader check, no fresh unlink, callback unconditioned, or the old cap-only message).

held_answer no longer acts on the snapshot it was handed. When the record it was given says 'starting' and the settle lock is found free, it re-reads the record: a live start call writes 'running' before it releases the settle lock, so only a record still 'starting' once the lock is free is a start call killed mid-settle; a fresh read that says 'running' takes the running branch (answered at the same commit, or replaced at another commit), and anything else goes to the stop-by-pid stale path as before. The settled part of _held_answer is unchanged. Test: test_held_answer_decides_on_a_read_after_the_probe starts a real product, hands _held_answer a 'starting' snapshot of the running record while the live product holds the lock, and asserts the answer of the running record is returned with code 0 and the product process is still alive afterwards. It fails against the pre-fix code, which treated the snapshot as stale, stopped the healthy product and returned None.

Both admission refusals now name the bar that was applied and keep the cap in the text: attach raises 'the record would be N bytes, over the 3872-byte limit (the 4000-byte cap less 128 bytes kept for later writes)' and env._launch_locked's refusal has the same form. Tests: test_record_over_the_headroom_is_refused_before_anything_is_written now captures the ValueError and asserts the limit phrase, the cap phrase and the measured size; test_start_refuses_an_oversize_product_record additionally asserts the limit phrase beside the cap. Both fail against the old cap-only messages.
